shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures dropped to a four-week low on Thursday on mounting hopes for a recovery in grain exports from the Black Sea region, analysts said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures dropped to a four-week low on Thursday on mounting hopes for a recovery in grain exports from the Black Sea region, analysts said.
Renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Ukraine war kept traders' attention on the outlook for Black Sea shipments.
Turkey said it stepped up efforts to re-establish a Black Sea grain corridor and received a positive response from Ukraine.
Cargo movements in the Black Sea region are at a near standstill due to heavy attacks on ships and port infrastructure by Russia and Ukraine.
Grain markets came under additional pressure as the dollar touched a two-month high, making US farm goods look more expensive to importers.

The US Department of Agriculture said net US wheat export sales in the week ended September 17 totaled 267,600 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year. A Reuters poll of analysts estimated sales of 350,000 and 600,000 tons.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed down 1-1/2 cents at $7.07 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last down 4-3/4 cents at $7.67 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was 9-1/2 cents lower at $7.20-1/4 a bushel.
